title: The Particle Report
brief: A customer of Meridian Microworks reports particle defects above limit on 30 percent of wafers from shipped lot {{lot}}. They require a containment response within 24 hours. You have 12 visit points to contain, find the cause, and respond.

actions.label: Lots shipped in the same week
General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: Complaint CQ-88 for {{lot}} was logged within 1 hour with the customer's maps.
4 other lots passed final clean in the same 2 days and shipped to 3 customers; none are on hold or notified.
evidence.whyItMatters: Containment must include output made under the same conditions.
evidence.missedExplanation: Check what else ran in the same window.

evidence.text: Particle counts in bay 3 exceeded the action limit for 6 hours during {{lot}}; no response was recorded.
evidence.whyItMatters: Environmental excursions must be responded to.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read environment logs for the lot's time window.

evidence.text: Filter change for bay 3 was due 3 weeks before the excursion; record shows "postponed, no parts".
evidence.missedExplanation: Check maintenance status of environment controls.

evidence.text: Final clean chemistry log shows bath changes on schedule.
evidence.missedExplanation: Conforming evidence that narrows the cause.

evidence.text: Technician: "The bay alarm kept going so we muted it." Mute log shows 2 mutes.
evidence.whyItMatters: Muting alarms without response weakens the control.

evidence.text: Outgoing inspection checked 2 wafers of 25 from {{lot}}; both passed.
evidence.whyItMatters: Release checks must be able to detect the problem, especially after an excursion.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask whether the sample could catch the problem.

evidence.text: Sampling plan SP-4 has no tightened sampling after an environment excursion.
evidence.whyItMatters: Verification arrangements should respond to known risks.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read the sampling plan for triggers.

evidence.text: Shipping boxes are qualified for particle cleanliness; record current.
The packing bench has a fan.
evidence.whyItMatters: The bench is in a controlled packing area with an approved fan.

evidence.text: Plants in the office outside the cleanroom.

options: Containment of all 5 lots from the excursion window with customers notified, the immediate cause (bay 3 excursion with overdue filter), actions with dates, and a contact
A statement that outgoing inspection passed
A request to clean the wafers at the customer
decisions.rationale: The customer needs to see exposure limited and the cause addressed.

containment: Hold and notify for all 5 lots processed during the excursion
correction: Re-inspect held wafers at 100 percent and disposition as authorized
cause: Filter maintenance was postponed, alarms were muted without response, and sampling has no excursion trigger
corrective: Escalate postponed filter changes, require a response before an alarm can be muted, and tighten sampling after excursions
effectiveness: Monitor excursion responses and particle complaints for six months

debriefText.found: You contained by time window, not just by lot.
debriefText.missed: Environment logs for the lot's time window often explain particle problems.
debriefText.falseFinding: Approved equipment and areas outside the cleanroom are not findings.
